summary: Kenya gets about 90% of its capacity from renewables, a third of it from independent power producers. A freeze on new PPAs was lifted with a move to competitive auctions, but the auction rules are still unclear. There are no foreign exchange controls.

access.reason: New PPAs are allowed again, but through a competitive auction system whose rules investors are still waiting to see.

terms.reason: Local costs may be paid in shillings while foreign debt can be serviced in hard currency, after a proposal for shilling-only contracts was dropped.

ownership.reason: Kenya repealed exchange controls in 1993, and funds from investment can be converted and transferred freely.

stability.reason: Contract changes now need regulator approval to stop informal renegotiation, and earlier projects face uncertainty.

direction.reason: The freeze on new PPAs has been lifted.

stability.reason: Rules ending the KPLC distribution monopoly were introduced in 2024.

direction.reason: 2024 changes seek to open transmission and distribution.

events.title: Rules introduced to end the KPLC and KETRACO monopolies
